summary: SSE reconnect behind corporate WAF rewrites chunk boundaries and truncates closing XML tag for rich attachment, footer omitted
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed truncated rich-attachment payloads after an SSE reconnect while behind a corporate WAF. The client-side parser reports an unclosed XML tag and the final footer block is missing.

Impact:
Several Acme Logistics end-users saw incomplete shipment reports (missing closing XML tag on <report> attachment), which caused downstream processing to reject the payload. Approximately 12% of streaming requests for this customer in us-east in the last 24h show similar symptoms.

Environment:
- Customer on Dedicated tier in prod-us-east behind a corporate WAF (third-party) and their NAT/proxy.
- Client: in-house web app using SSE polyfill, reconnect logic enabled.
- Model: redwood-v1-medium via streaming chat endpoint.

Observed behavior:
- Stream starts and emits most fragments correctly. After an edge failover or WAF idle-probe, the client reconnects and resumes. The server-side logs show a resume delta containing the tail fragment, but the final closing XML tag is absent in the stitched output. The UI shows truncated XML and missing footer block.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should reassemble all fragments so that XML attachments end with a valid closing tag and the footer is present.

Notes on uniqueness of the failure:
- Affected payloads are XML attachments embedded in the streamed deltas (large multi-chunk attachments). The truncation consistently affects the last 8-40 bytes (closing tag and trailing whitespace). This pattern differs from simple duplicate-prefix or missing-final-event issues observed previously: here the final bytes are removed, not reordered or duplicated.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a client to stream a long XML attachment via SSE to the Redwood streaming endpoint behind a proxy/WAF that performs chunked transfer rewrite.
2) Simulate an idle-probe or small failover at the edge (close the socket on an upstream LB) to force a reconnect/resume from the client-side SSE polyfill.
3) Observe the reassembled attachment on the client; check for missing closing XML tag (e.g., missing '</report>').
4) Capture edge and server traces (see trace id pattern below) and compare the server-emitted final fragment to the client-observed tail.
5) Repeat with direct (no-WAF) path — issue does not reproduce when WAF/proxy is bypassed.
logs: customer-provided: client console shows parser error: 'XMLParser: unexpected EOF at line 1, column 1432'
edge-proxy: connection reset by upstream (idle-probe) at 2026-03-10T17:04:12Z
serving-runtime: resume-delta: final_chunk_base64='PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvb...' (base64 ends earlier than expected)
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): reproduced with Acme test app behind their corporate WAF; bypassing WAF yields correct final tag.

Edge hypothesis: chunk-boundary rewrite or chunk coalescing at WAF is dropping trailing bytes when connection is handed off during idle probe. This differs from simple reordering bugs — bytes are missing at the end of the stream assembly.
Captured pcap at customer edge shows WAF rewriting chunked boundaries; last chunk size header omitted during an upstream RST+reconnect sequence.

Server traces show we emitted the final bytes before connection closure — server-side assembly looks correct (trace-0ab12c34). Problem appears in transport during reconnect and chunked-transfer reassembly by the WAF/edge.
Checked proxy headers: found evidence of 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' header rewrite and a suspicious zero-length chunk sequence in one failover case.

Related tickets: SUP-311223 and SUP-214159 reference similar resume edge cases behind proxies, but this one consistently removes the trailing closing tag rather than duplicating or misordering fragments.
Customer provided corp-WAF vendor logs; vendor notes 'chunk coalescing optimization' on for that appliance version. They are reproducing internally with a similar workload.
comments: Support (Ava Patel) 2026-03-10: Opened with priority P1 after customer reported automated downstream failures. Attached customer logs and sample payloads.
SRE (Diego Morales) 2026-03-11: Collected server-side traces (trace-0ab12c34). Serving runtime shows final fragment emitted. Asking edge team to check proxy handoff traces and LB logs.

Edge eng (Lina Chen) 2026-03-11: Found LB handoff at 17:04:12Z that preceded an upstream RST. WAF appliance appears to rewrite chunk headers when connection is reset, resulting in a dropped terminal chunk. Engaging WAF vendor.
Customer (Acme, Thomas Reed) 2026-03-11: Verified that bypassing their WAF removes the symptom. They've provided a test harness and allowed a short maintenance window to test mitigations.

Support (Ava Patel) 2026-03-12: Applied temporary workaround: recommend customer disable WAF chunk coalescing or enable connection draining to avoid mid-chunk RST. Customer confirmed improved results during maintenance window.

Edge eng (Lina Chen) 2026-03-12: Proposing a server-side mitigation: emit a final explicit 'end-of-attachment' control event that is idempotent on resume. This will be discussed with product and runtime teams for risk/release planning.
root_cause: Interaction between corporate WAF chunked-transfer rewrite/coalescing and edge connection handoffs: terminal chunk size header was lost during a mid-stream upstream reset, leading to dropped final bytes on client-side assembly.
workaround: Advise customer to disable WAF chunk coalescing / enable connection draining on their WAF or LB. If not possible, enable short client-side post-resume validation and request re-fetch of attachment via REST endpoint as fallback.
resolution_notes: Temporary: customer disabled chunk coalescing and confirmed attachments now include closing tag. Long-term: engineering will evaluate emitting an explicit idempotent 'attachment-terminator' control delta on the streaming channel and add guard logic in the edge proxy to preserve zero-length final chunks. Follow-up EPIC to be created if approved.
next_steps: 1) Edge team to add safeguards in proxy to avoid omitting final zero-length chunk headers during handoffs (owner: Lina Chen).
2) Product/Runtime to review streaming protocol extension for explicit attachment terminator event (owner: Marcus Liu).
3) Coordinate with customer to validate fix in staging and then schedule a controlled deploy (timebox: 2 sprints).
4) Update Stream Resume Runbook (confluence) with WAF-related troubleshooting steps and the new diagnostic trace ids to collect.
